tradition.name: Norwegian Latin school roundhand (engelsk-latinsk Haandskrift)
tradition.notes: English roundhand as taught in Christiania in 1849: very steep (the plate's own slant guide is 45 degrees), pointed-pen shading on the downstrokes, long hairline connectors rising from the baseline, plain unlooped ascenders (b d h k l, the hairline climbs inside the stem), looped descenders (g j y, long s), knotted top exits on b v w, v and w begun with an overturn like n, p with a half-ascender stem, q with a crossed descender, and long s still in use. Capitals are flourished roundhand forms with ball terminals and bottom-left curls; they do not join.

source.name: Brandt, Skjønskrivningsregler for de engelsk-latinske og gothiske eller norske Haandskrifter (1849), plates of the Latin small letters and capitals
source.credit: Brandt (writing master at the Borgerskole in Christiania), Skjønskrivningsregler for de engelsk-latinske og gothiske eller norske Haandskrifter (Christiania: P. F. Steensballe, 1849). Nasjonalbiblioteket; public domain
